lead: The 8051 is an 8-bit microcontroller: CPU, memory and I/O on one chip. It uses Harvard architecture, so code and data have separate address spaces. Code ROM is 4 KB, data RAM 128 bytes, and the special function registers (SFRs) that drive the peripherals occupy their own 128 bytes. Fixed pins and a fixed register map keep this old design inside ATMs, washing machines and lift controllers.
prereq: You need Harvard versus von Neumann organization, and microprocessor versus microcontroller, from Unit 1, Foundations.

blocks.text: The core is an 8-bit CPU with an 8-bit ALU and working registers A and B. Code comes from 4 KB of on-chip ROM at 0000-0FFF; data comes from 128 bytes of RAM at 00-7F. Two 16-bit timer/counters, one UART, an interrupt controller and four 8-bit ports complete the chip.

Harvard shows in the buses. A fetch from external program memory drives PSEN (program store enable); fetches from internal ROM do not. Data reads and writes drive RD or WR. So code address 0000 and data address 00 are different places, and the opcode decides which space you mean. That is why MOVC and MOVX sit beside plain MOV.
The 8051 comes in a 40-pin DIP. Pin 40 is Vcc (+5 V), pin 20 is GND.
Port 0 (P0.0-P0.7) is the multiplexed low bus: AD0-AD7 carry the low address byte, then the data byte. Port 2 (P2.0-P2.7) supplies A8-A15. Port 1 is plain I/O.
Port 3 pins have second jobs: P3.0 RXD and P3.1 TXD (serial), P3.2 INT0 and P3.3 INT1 (external interrupts), P3.4 T0 and P3.5 T1 (timer inputs), P3.6 WR and P3.7 RD (external data strobes).

Control pins: XTAL1 and XTAL2 take the crystal, often 12 MHz. RST is active high. EA high selects internal ROM; EA low forces external code. PSEN is the external code read strobe; ALE latches the low address byte out of Port 0.
Pin numbering matters for wiring: P0.0 is pin 39, P1.0 is pin 1, and the control pins sit at the top of the package.

sections.h3: Memory map: three spaces, no overlap

blocks.text: Code space 0000-0FFF holds the program; execution starts at 0000 on reset.

Data RAM 00-7F is reachable directly and indirectly. The lowest 32 bytes are four register banks of eight: 00-07, 08-0F, 10-17, 18-1F. PSW bits RS1:RS0 pick the active bank. Bytes 20-2F are bit-addressable: 16 bytes × 8 bits = 128 bit addresses, numbered 00-7F.

SFR space 80-FF is reachable only by direct address; RAM 80-FF is reachable only indirectly. So the same number names an SFR in direct mode and a RAM byte in indirect mode. On a plain 8051 nothing is at 80-FF but SFRs; parts in the 8052 family add a second 128 bytes of RAM there, indirect only.
SFR addresses: ACC E0, B F0, PSW D0, SP 81, DPL 82, DPH 83, P0 80, P1 90, P2 A0, P3 B0, IE A8, IP B8, TCON 88, TMOD 89, TL0 8A, TL1 8B, TH0 8C, TH1 8D, SCON 98, SBUF 99, PCON 87.

figure.caption: The CPU reaches ROM, RAM and SFRs by separate paths. SFRs are the only route to timers, UART, interrupt logic and ports.

examples.question: Data RAM byte 0x2A holds 0x84. Find the bit addresses of bit 2 and bit 7, and the value at each.
steps: Bit-addressable RAM starts at 0x20 and gives bit addresses 0x00-0x7F.
Offset of 0x2A from 0x20 is 10 bytes, so its bit base is 10 × 8 = 80 = 0x50.
examples.answer: Bit 2 is bit address 0x52 (82) and bit 7 is 0x57 (87); both hold 1.

traps: On an 8052, direct address 80-FF selects an SFR, never upper RAM. To read upper RAM byte 80H you must load the address into R0 or R1 and use @R0. A plain 8051 has no upper RAM.
EA low or floating makes the CPU fetch from the external bus, so the chip looks dead with a correct program inside. Tie EA to Vcc for internal ROM.
SP resets to 07, so the first PUSH goes to 08 — inside register bank 1. Move SP to 0x30 (30H) so the first push lands at 0x31 and all four banks stay free.
Bit address 0x52 and byte address 0x52 are different objects; the instruction picks (SETB versus MOV).

quiz.q: Give the SFR address of PSW and of SP.
Which port pins carry RXD and TXD?
quiz.a: P3.0 is RXD, P3.1 is TXD.

quiz.q: Why can code address 0000 and data address 00 hold different bytes?
quiz.a: Harvard organization: separate spaces and strobes. PSEN selects code, RD and WR select data, and the opcode decides which space is meant.

quiz.q: After reset SP = 07. Where does the first PUSH store, and what is SP after?
quiz.a: SP increments to 08, the byte goes to RAM address 08, SP stays 08. Address 08 is in register bank 1, so that bank cannot be in use.

quiz.q: RAM byte 0x25 holds 0x01. Give the bit address of bit 0 and say whether it is set.
quiz.a: Base = (0x25 − 0x20) × 8 = 40 = 0x28; bit 0 is 0x28. 0x01 has bit 0 = 1, so address 0x28 reads 1.

quiz.q: On an 8052, why does MOV A, 0A0h not read upper RAM byte 0A0H?
quiz.a: Direct addressing above 7F always lands in SFR space; 0A0 is P2. Upper RAM is indirect only, so load 0A0 into R0 and use MOV A, @R0. A plain 8051 has no upper RAM at that address.

beyond: Not for the exam. Modern clones finish one machine cycle per clock instead of twelve, add a 16-bit multiply, extra timers, ADC and CAN, and reach tens of MIPS. The 8051 core is also a standard block inside ASICs and FPGAs for housekeeping, because 4 KB of code goes a long way. Search: '8051 machine cycle timing', '8051 IP core FPGA'.
